content: Famotidine is a medication prescribed to treat ulcers, which are sores on the lining of the stomach or small intestine. It is also used to manage gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and conditions where the stomach produces excessive acid, such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, a condition caused by tumors in the pancreas or small intestine that lead to increased stomach acid production. Over-the-counter famotidine is used to prevent and treat heartburn caused by acid indigestion or sour stomach, often triggered by consuming certain foods or drinks. Famotidine belongs to a class of medications known as H2 blockers, which work by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Prescription famotidine is available as tablets and liquid suspensions, taken orally. It is typically taken once daily at bedtime or two to four times a day, depending on the condition being treated. Over-the-counter famotidine is available as tablets, chewable tablets, and capsules, also taken orally. It is usually taken once or twice a day. To prevent symptoms, it should be taken 15 to 60 minutes before consuming foods or drinks that may cause heartburn. Always follow the instructions on your prescription or the package label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take famotidine exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Shake the liquid form well for 5 to 10 seconds before each use to ensure even mixing. Swallow tablets and capsules with a full glass of water. Chewable tablets should be thoroughly chewed before swallowing, followed by a full glass of water. Do not take more than two tablets, capsules, or chewable tablets of over-the-counter famotidine within 24 hours, and do not use it for longer than two weeks unless directed by your doctor. If symptoms of heartburn, acid indigestion, or sour stomach persist for more than two weeks, stop taking the medication and consult your doctor. Famotidine may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking famotidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to famotidine, cimetidine (Tagamet), nizatidine (Axid), ranitidine (Zantac), or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially other medications for heartburn. Do not take over-the-counter famotidine with any other heartburn medications unless directed by your doctor. Inform your doctor if you have phenylketonuria (PKU), a condition that requires a specific diet to prevent mental retardation, or if you have or have ever had difficulty swallowing or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking famotidine, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking famotidine. If you miss a dose of prescription famotidine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Over-the-counter famotidine is usually taken as needed. If your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly, follow the same guidelines for missed doses. Famotidine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include headache, dizziness, constipation, diarrhea, and fussiness in babies taking the medication. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, include hives, skin rash, itching, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, hoarseness, and difficulty breathing or swallowing. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while taking this medication to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store famotidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Do not allow the liquid form to freeze. Discard any outdated or no longer needed medication, and dispose of unused liquid famotidine after 30 days. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
